video.title: I Tested This "Genius" Side Hustle (Is It A Goldmine?)

summary: Chris Koerner tests a disc golf 'ace challenge' inspired by a New Zealand floating golf green that reportedly nets $500k a year: players pay for throws and win $1,000 for a hole-in-one. In a Dallas park, security stopped him charging or paying out, so revenue was $0. At DFW Disc Golf in Arlington, with proceeds going to the owner's homeless charity, players threw from 95 feet and one skilled player aced it after about 180 shots, with $780 in fees against the $1,000 prize. Key takeaway: skill-challenge businesses are a statistics problem, so test for free to measure hit rates by distance and skill, then price accordingly and partner with tournaments and shops.

ideas.name: Disc golf hole-in-one cash challenge
ideas.one_liner: Charge $5-10 per throw for a chance to ace a disc golf basket from 65-95 feet and win $1,000.
ideas.business_model: pay-per-attempt game of skill with a cash prize
ideas.customer: Disc golfers at shops, tournaments and parks
ideas.problem: Players want a fun, high-stakes side game
ideas.offer: $10 for one throw / $20 for three throws (tested), suggested $5 for one / $10 for three, $1,000 prize for an ace

pricing.notes: Prize $1,000; pricing must be set from measured hit probability by distance and skill level.

acquisition_channels.details: Partnered with DFW Disc Golf shop in Arlington, Texas, donating proceeds to the owner's nonprofit; recommends partnering with tournaments, shops, apps.

quote.text: the way to do this business is to partner with disc golf tournaments, disc golf shops, disc golf enthusiasts, disc golf apps
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

acquisition_channels.details: Signs advertising a $1,000 cash reward in a busy park; park security stopped charging/paying out.

ideas.delivery: Operator sets up basket and throw line, collects fees and tracks attempts; pays prize on an ace.
unit_economics_claims: Shop test: ~180 throws before an ace by a skilled player; $780 owed in entry fees vs $1,000 prize
ideas.startup_cost: Basket, discs ($12-25 each), signs, prize money reserve

uk_applicability.notes: UK: genuine games of skill are generally outside the Gambling Act 2005, but prize competitions need care (a skill test that most cannot pass may be judged chance); public parks need council permission; disc golf is niche in the UK.

risks: Venue permission (park security shut it down)
Variance: an early ace wipes out revenue

tactics.name: Calibrate skill-game odds before charging
steps: Run the challenge for free first
Record each attempt's distance, player skill level and outcome
Set distance and price so expected payouts stay below revenue
Recommended: $5 per throw or $10 for three at a long enough distance

quote.text: I recommend doing it for free to get those numbers down
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: Go where the niche already gathers
steps: Skip general public parks where few know the sport
Set up at specialty shops and tournaments as a side show
Partner with the venue (e.g. donate proceeds to the owner's cause)

tactics.name: Get venue permission before charging
steps: Confirm park rules on charging and cash prizes
Use private land or partner venues

quote.text: They don't want us charging. They don't want us giving away free money

warnings.warning: Too short a distance invites skilled 'pool sharks'.

warnings.warning: Targeting skilled players raises both participation and win probability.
UK note (extractor): prize-for-skill games must be genuine skill to avoid being classed as gambling under the Gambling Act 2005.

lessons.lesson: Skill-game viability is a probability problem: distance, skill level and price are the variables.

quote.text: this is math. This is just pure statistics
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

lessons.lesson: The house always wins over the long run once odds are known.

quote.text: People go to the casino and they win sometimes, but the house always wins over the long run
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

lessons.lesson: Collect data even from a failed test; it informs pricing.

quote.text: Even if we don't charge though, we still get a gauge for how much we could make
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

lessons.lesson: Pick a venue where the audience understands the product.

quote.text: Most people had never heard of what disc golf is. That just didn't work
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

lessons.lesson: Partnering with a local cause can unlock venue access and goodwill.

evidence_quality.rationale: First-hand one-day experiment with real numbers but a tiny sample, and the NZ profit figure is hearsay.
